summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter, and an upstream status probe. It registers all three routes in main.go.

findings.title: SQL injection in user search
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter into the SQL text with Sprintf. The value is not escaped or bound.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can read or change any row in the database with a crafted name.
findings.fix: Pass name to QueryContext as a bound parameter instead of formatting it into the query.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex stays locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count takes h.mu, then returns early when key is empty without unlocking it.
findings.consequence: One request without a key leaves the lock held, so every later GET /count request hangs forever.
findings.fix: Validate key before taking the lock, or unlock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Nil response dereferenced on fetch error
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil.
findings.consequence: Whenever the upstream is unreachable, GET /upstream panics instead of returning 502.
findings.fix: Move the deferred Close below the error check.

findings.title: New handlers have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream, but the repository contains no Go test files.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions in these handlers, including the locking and error paths.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests that cover each handler, including the empty key and unreachable upstream cases.

dropped.reason: This is the same SQL injection on the same line that the c1 finding already reports.
